requirement: An import stopped by two-factor sign-in, a refusal in another language, a cookie the site renews, or an upload the server finds too large or forbids names that reason, claims a wrong password only on a message it recognises, and carries a database's binary columns byte for byte

oracle.ref: PR #1483 (fix); fix evidence: PR 1483. Before the fix two-factor sign-in, a refusal in a non-English backend, a lost session cookie and a 413 on the upload read as invalid_credential, unreachable or install_failed, and binary columns were changed in the dump. Each case below was written red before the fix and is green after it; no real customer site or real Joomla/WordPress stand was rerun after the last review fixes.
oracle.invariant: Exit code 0 and `# fail 0`. Two-factor (import-signin-data): a Joomla 3 login page with a Secret Key field and a Joomla 4+ captive MFA page after the right password are mfa_required, the password posted once; Joomla 4.0/4.1 secret-key messages in the script options are read in both wordings. Joomla sign-in refusals (import-signin-data): the page's messages are read first; a wrong password, no administrator access or a secret-key refusal counts only when the message matches English or the site's own administrator language file (joomla.ini, its override, INI comments, `_QQ_` and entities decoded); a language tag never builds a path outside the language folder; language reads stop at two requests and at the first 401/403/429 or firewall page; anything not recognised keeps invalid_credential with diagnostic check message_unread and its own customer sentence. WordPress sign-in refusals (wordpress-login, handover-lifecycle): only core's English wrong-password or unknown-user sentence is invalid_credential; a translated core error, a translated lockout carrying core's lost-password link, or a captcha widget with no error naming it is message_unread at login_post; the importer error survives a cached read. Cookies (import-signin-data): the cookie jar keeps every cookie of one site with its path and Secure flag across a renewing login POST and a bare-host to www redirect, and drops cookies of other sites. Upload refused (import-signin-data, wordpress-install): an HTTP 413 on the Joomla or WordPress package upload is upload_too_large with diagnostic {at: upload_install, check: too_large, status: 413, path}; a 403 on the same POST stops too (Joomla: install_forbidden on Joomla's own page, otherwise admin_gate; WordPress: install_failed with check forbidden on its own wp_die page, otherwise blocked_by_firewall with check server_denied); after either, Joomla asks only the URL road (#1568: the upload road goes first) and the 413 or 403 still decides when it does not install; WordPress asks nothing more. Data (import-signin-data): a binary (BLOB) column survives the dump byte for byte; the new diagnostic checks and paths are known to both the worker and the web closed lists.
oracle.productSourceGap: no product file is imported, read or run through a supported form in the command's test files (see tests/qa/layers/unit/lib/sources.mjs)
